ucs.title: [LLM] Salt Typhoon (FamousSparrow/Earth Estries) SparrowDoor / HemiGate sideloading via signed AV or Microsoft host binary
ucs.description: Hunts the trademark Salt Typhoon initial-execution primitive: a legitimately signed K7 Computing AV binary, mscorsvw, or other host EXE running from a non-vendor directory (typically %ProgramData%, %Public%, or a user-writable folder) and loading a same-directory DLL. ESET (FamousSparrow) and Trend Micro (Earth Estries) have both documented this exact loader chain for SparrowDoor, Crowdoor and HemiGate.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_hash) as host_hash values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("k7tsecurity.exe","k7tsmain.exe","k7tsmngr.exe","k7ui.exe","mscorsvw.exe","setres.exe","ihostingservice.exe","esmertec.exe","avastsvc.exe","bdservicehost.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path | rename Processes.* as * | where NOT match(process_path, "(?i)^[A-Z]:\\\\Program Files( \\(x86\\))?\\\\") AND NOT match(process_path, "(?i)^[A-Z]:\\\\Windows\\\\(System32|SysWOW64|WinSxS|assembly)\\\\") | join type=left dest process_path [ | tstats summariesonly=t count as dll_writes values(Filesystem.file_name) as dropped_dlls from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="*.dll" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path | rename Filesystem.* as * | eval process_path = replace(file_path,"\\\\[^\\\\]+$","") ] | where isnotnull(dropped_dlls) | table firstTime, lastTime, dest, user, parent_name, process_name, process_path, host_hash, dropped_dlls, cmdline | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - firstTime
ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let SideloadHosts = dynamic(["k7tsecurity.exe","k7tsmain.exe","k7tsmngr.exe","k7ui.exe","mscorsvw.exe","setres.exe","ihostingservice.exe","esmertec.exe","avastsvc.exe","bdservicehost.exe"]);
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (SideloadHosts)
| where FileName endswith ".dll"
| extend HostDir = tolower(InitiatingProcessFolderPath)
| extend DllDir  = tolower(FolderPath)
// host binary running outside its vendor install path (Salt Typhoon stages to ProgramData / Public / user dirs)
| where not(HostDir startswith "c:\\program files")
    and not(HostDir startswith "c:\\windows\\system32")
    and not(HostDir startswith "c:\\windows\\syswow64")
    and not(HostDir startswith "c:\\windows\\winsxs")
// classic sideload: loaded DLL lives in the same folder as the signed host
| where DllDir == HostDir
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
    | project DropTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DroppedPath = tolower(FolderPath), DroppedName = FileName,
              Dropper = InitiatingProcessFileName, DropperCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine
  ) on $left.DeviceId == $right.DeviceId and $left.DllDir == $right.DroppedPath and $left.FileName =~ $right.DroppedName
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          HostBinary = InitiatingProcessFileName, HostPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, HostSha256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256,
          LoadedDll = FileName, LoadedDllPath = FolderPath, LoadedDllSha256 = SHA256,
          DropTime, Dropper, DropperCmd
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let SideloadHosts = dynamic(["k7tsecurity.exe","k7tsmain.exe","k7tsmngr.exe","k7ui.exe","mscorsvw.exe","setres.exe","ihostingservice.exe","esmertec.exe","avastsvc.exe","bdservicehost.exe"]);
// Sysmon EventID 7 (image-load) shipped to Sentinel via WindowsEvent / Event
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where Source =~ "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 7
| extend ed = parse_xml(EventData)
| extend Image = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[3].['#text']),
         ImageLoaded = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[5].['#text']),
         Signed = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[10].['#text']),
         SignatureStatus = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[12].['#text'])
| extend HostName = tolower(tostring(split(Image, "\\")[-1]))
| where HostName in~ (SideloadHosts)
| extend HostDir = tolower(strcat_array(array_slice(split(Image, "\\"), 0, -2), "\\")),
         DllDir  = tolower(strcat_array(array_slice(split(ImageLoaded, "\\"), 0, -2), "\\"))
| where not(HostDir startswith "c:\\program files")
    and not(HostDir startswith "c:\\windows\\system32")
    and not(HostDir startswith "c:\\windows\\syswow64")
    and not(HostDir startswith "c:\\windows\\winsxs")
| where DllDir == HostDir
| where Signed =~ "false" or SignatureStatus !~ "Valid"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Image, ImageLoaded, Signed, SignatureStatus
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:7 @Image:(*\\k7tsecurity.exe OR *\\K7TSecurity.exe OR *\\k7tsmain.exe OR *\\k7ui.exe OR *\\K7UI.exe OR *\\mscorsvw.exe OR *\\MSCorSvw.exe OR *\\setres.exe OR *\\ihostingservice.exe OR *\\esmertec.exe OR *\\bdservicehost.exe) @ImageLoaded:*.dll -@Image:(*\\Program?Files\\* OR *\\PROGRAM?FILES\\* OR *\\Windows\\System32\\* OR *\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\* OR *\\Windows\\WinSxS\\*) (@Signed:false OR @SignatureStatus:(Unavailable OR Invalid))
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(k7tsecurity|k7tsmain|k7tsmngr|k7ui|mscorsvw|setres|ihostingservice|esmertec|avastsvc|bdservicehost)\.exe$/i
| NOT regex("(?i)^[a-z]:\\\\program files", field=ImageFileName)
| NOT regex("(?i)^[a-z]:\\\\windows\\\\(system32|syswow64|winsxs)", field=ImageFileName)
| HostDir := replace(ImageFileName, regex="\\\\[^\\\\]+$", replacement="")
| join({#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\.dll$/i}, field=aid, key=ContextProcessId, include=[DroppedDll:=TargetFileName, DropTime:=_time], mode=left)
| DroppedDllDir := replace(DroppedDll, regex="\\\\[^\\\\]+$", replacement="")
| test(DroppedDllDir == HostDir)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, SHA256HashData, DroppedDll], function=[count(), min(_time, as=firstSeen), max(_time, as=lastSeen)])
ucs.rationale: Salt Typhoon's intrusion sets (FamousSparrow→SparrowDoor; Earth Estries→HemiGate/Crowdoor; GhostEmperor→Demodex loader) all use the same staging pattern: a small ZIP/cab is dropped to a non-vendor path, then a signed host EXE (most often a K7 Computing AV component or a stripped Microsoft .NET binary) is launched from that staging folder so its co-located malicious DLL satisfies the loader's searc

ucs.title: [LLM] Salt Typhoon comsvcs.dll LSASS dump chained to WMI/PsExec lateral movement
ucs.description: Hunts the canonical Salt Typhoon post-exploitation pivot documented by Trend Micro across the Earth Estries telecom intrusions: rundll32.exe invoking comsvcs.dll's MiniDump export against lsass.exe, followed within minutes on the same host by wmic /node, PsExec, or remote scheduled-task creation. This pair (T1003.001 → T1047/T1021.002) is the actor's bread-and-butter credential-pivot chain inside telco/government environments.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as dump_time values(Processes.process) as dump_cmd values(Processes.user) as dump_user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*" AND (Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*#24*") AND Processes.process="*lsass*" by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name | rename Processes.* as * | join type=inner dest [ | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as lat_time values(Processes.process) as lat_cmd values(Processes.process_name) as lat_tool values(Processes.user) as lat_user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*" AND Processes.process="*process*call*create*") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexec64.exe","paexec.exe")) OR (Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" AND Processes.process="*/s *" AND Processes.process="*/create*") OR (Processes.parent_process_name="services.exe" AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") AND Processes.process="*ADMIN$*") by Processes.dest | rename Processes.* as * ] | where lat_time >= dump_time AND lat_time <= dump_time + 900 | eval delay_sec = lat_time - dump_time | table dump_time, lat_time, delay_sec, dest, dump_user, dump_cmd, lat_user, lat_tool, lat_cmd | convert ctime(dump_time) ctime(lat_time) | sort - dump_time
ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMinutes = 15m;
let LsassDumps = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName =~ "rundll32.exe"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "comsvcs.dll"
        and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("MiniDump","#24")
        and ProcessCommandLine has "lsass"
    | project DumpTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName,
              DumpUser = AccountName, DumpCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
              DumpParent = InitiatingProcessFileName;
let Lateral = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("process call create","process create"))
        or (FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexec64.exe","paexec.exe"))
        or (FileName =~ "schtasks.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/s " and ProcessCommandLine has "/create")
        or (FileName =~ "powershell.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WMIMethod","Invoke-CimMethod","New-PSSession","Enter-PSSession"))
    | project LatTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName,
              LatUser = AccountName, LatTool = FileName, LatCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
LsassDumps
| join kind=inner Lateral on DeviceId
| where LatTime between (DumpTime .. DumpTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', LatTime, DumpTime)
| where DumpUser !endswith "$"
| project DumpTime, LatTime, DelaySec, DeviceName,
          DumpUser, DumpCmd, DumpParent,
          LatUser, LatTool, LatCmd
| order by DumpTime desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMinutes = 15m;
let LsassDumps = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith @"\rundll32.exe"
    | where CommandLine has "comsvcs.dll"
        and CommandLine has_any ("MiniDump","#24")
        and CommandLine has "lsass"
    | project DumpTime = TimeGenerated, Computer,
              DumpUser = SubjectUserName, DumpCmd = CommandLine,
              DumpParent = ParentProcessName;
let Lateral = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where (NewProcessName endswith @"\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:" and CommandLine has "process call create")
        or (NewProcessName endswith @"\psexec.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\psexec64.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\paexec.exe")
        or (NewProcessName endswith @"\schtasks.exe" and CommandLine has "/s " and CommandLine has "/create")
        or (NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WMIMethod","Invoke-CimMethod","New-PSSession"))
    | project LatTime = TimeGenerated, Computer,
              LatUser = SubjectUserName, LatTool = NewProcessName, LatCmd = CommandLine;
LsassDumps
| join kind=inner Lateral on Computer
| where LatTime between (DumpTime .. DumpTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', LatTime, DumpTime)
| where DumpUser !endswith "$"
| project DumpTime, LatTime, DelaySec, Computer, DumpUser, DumpCmd, DumpParent, LatUser, LatTool, LatCmd
| order by DumpTime desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Salt Typhoon (Earth Estries / FamousSparrow) LSASS Dump via comsvcs.dll MiniDump
id: 7e2f5c91-d4b8-4a3e-9c1d-8a7f6b3d2e9c
status: experimental
description: Detects rundll32.exe invoking the comsvcs.dll MiniDump export against lsass.exe, a documented Salt Typhoon (G1045) credential-access primitive used in Earth Estries telecom intrusions.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1045/
  - https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/23/h/earth-estries-targets-government-tech-for-cyberespionage.html
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/31
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1003.001
  - attack.g1045
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith: '\rundll32.exe'
  selection_cmd_dll:
    CommandLine|contains: 'comsvcs.dll'
  selection_cmd_export:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'MiniDump'
      - '#24'
  selection_cmd_target:
    CommandLine|contains: 'lsass'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Extremely rare legitimate administrative dumping; investigate every hit
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\rundll32.exe OR *\\Rundll32.exe OR *\\RUNDLL32.EXE) @CommandLine:(*comsvcs.dll* OR *Comsvcs.dll* OR *COMSVCS.DLL*) (@CommandLine:*MiniDump* OR @CommandLine:*minidump* OR @CommandLine:*\#24*) (@CommandLine:*lsass* OR @CommandLine:*LSASS* OR @CommandLine:*Lsass*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\rundll32\.exe$/i CommandLine=/comsvcs\.dll/i CommandLine=/(MiniDump|#24)/i CommandLine=/lsass/i
| dump_aid := aid
| dump_time := _time
| dump_cmd := CommandLine
| dump_host := ComputerName
| dump_user := UserName
| join(query={#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ImageFileName=/\\wmic\.exe$/i CommandLine=/\/node:/i CommandLine=/process[\s]+call[\s]+create/i) OR ImageFileName=/\\psexec(64)?\.exe$/i OR (ImageFileName=/\\schtasks\.exe$/i CommandLine=/\/s\s/i CommandLine=/\/create/i) | lat_time := _time | lat_cmd := CommandLine | lat_tool := ImageFileName}, field=dump_aid, key=aid, include=[lat_time, lat_cmd, lat_tool])
| test(lat_time >= dump_time)
| test(lat_time <= dump_time + 900)
| delay_sec := lat_time - dump_time
| groupBy([dump_host, dump_user, dump_cmd, lat_tool, lat_cmd, delay_sec], function=count())
ucs.rationale: The comsvcs.dll MiniDump primitive is virtually never seen in benign administration — every documented use is malicious. Trend Micro's Earth Estries reports and CISA's 2024 telecom advisories specifically call out the rundll32+comsvcs+lsass pattern as Salt Typhoon's preferred LSASS dump technique because the binary is in-box and Microsoft-signed (it bypasses naïve PSExec/Mimikatz allow-lists). Pai
